newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares falter at 1,600 support, shed 3.18pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares falter at 1,600 support, shed 3.18pct.

text.p: Greek shares shed 3.18 percent and fell through the 1,600 support level, hurt by spiking short-term interbank rates on tighter liquidity conditions in the money market.

Stocks followed bonds which came under renewed selling pressure and gave up 50-100 basis points in price. They were hit by rising interbank rates that affected cost of carry and the FRN auction schedule which turned out heavier than the market expected it to be.
"The market was hit by rising interbank rates today," said Pavlos Vranas, managing director of Euroxx Securities.
Bond prices recovered some of the lost ground after the long end of the money market eased on drachma inflows, dealers said.
"Some of the pressure has been reduced but the problem has yet to dissapear for the stock market to take a breath of relief," Vranas said.

Traders also said market sentiment was dented today by the prospect of a halt in the rate of easing in consumer price inflation. Financial press reports pointed to a reduced scope for improvement in the inflation rate over the rest of this year.

"Today's financial press reports on more stubborn inflation in the coming months on the back of Thursday's higher-than-expected May CPI has given rise to a feeling of anti-climax," said Alexis Panagiotopoulos, broker at Intersec.

CPI inflation eased to 5.4 percent in May from 5.9 percent in April, but core inflation which does not include volatile food and energy prices was unchanged at 7.5 percent for the third consecutive month.
Selling pressure on state telecoms OTE which is headed for a large part-flotation and rights issue in the coming weeks continued to drive the stock's price lower, closing 175 drachmas lower at 6,965.
"Institutional investors would be delighted to see the strike price of the book-building process being set while the stock trades between 6,500 and 7,000 drachmas," Vranas said.
Increased supply of new shares arising from recent capital increases were also seen as a potential source of selling pressure.

"New shares arising from recent share capital increases are the first victims of a deterioration in psychology because they incorporate very large capital gains, taking the issue discount into account," Panagiotopoulos said.
Shares of ErgoBank were attacked today and Alpha Credit may also be affected in the near-term, he added.
From a technical point of view, the market was seen extending its drift after important support levels had been broken.
"The 1,600 support level was tested for the third time in the course of two months and was discredited," said Iakovos Diamantopoulos, an analyst at Hermes Brokerage.
The next important support level is the 1,520 to 1,550 band, he added.
The Athens general index settled 3.18 percent or 52.31 points to 1,592.35 from Thursday's close at 1,644.66.
It set an intra-day low at 1,579.22 at mid-session, nearly 4.0 percent lower than Thursday's close.
Banks and industrials led the market with respective losses of 3.3 and 3.4 percent. Turnover remained at moderate levels of 22.1 billion drachmas on volume of 4.5 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 194 to 35 with 11 shares unchanged on 240 traded.
